notes: The dataset ships one `text` column holding a two-turn chat. The first answer has the form 'Yes, it contains a vulnerability. It is classified as <label> and is related to the code:`<expr>`. In SWC it is mapped with: <swc>.' or 'No, it does not contain any vulnerabilities.'

The <label> vocabulary is 6 values across 205 rows, so labels parse exactly. The vocabulary is coarser than VULN_CATALOG: 'Missing Key Check' (72 rows) covers signer, owner, and pubkey-equality checks and is mapped to missing-owner-check, so ARES answering missing-signer-check on one of those rows scores as a false positive plus a false negative.
Severity is absent from the dataset. The values below are the VULN_CATALOG defaultSeverity of the mapped class and exist only to make the --by severity breakdown work.

Rows are function-level snippets, not whole programs, and 'Integer Flow' rows include cases already guarded by checked_* arithmetic. Treat a score on this dataset as a signal about one label vocabulary, not as ARES's audit quality.
A row labeled clean contributes no ground truth rows; anything ARES reports on it counts as a false positive.
clean_answer_prefix: No, it does not contain any vulnerabilities
